newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru blames subway gassing on followers.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru blames subway gassing on followers.

text.p: The guru of a Japanese doomsday cult accused of the Tokyo subway gas attack told a court hearing on Thursday he tried to stop his followers from carrying out the attack but failed.

"I ordered (top disciple Hideo) Murai to stop on the night of the 18th and I ordered (senior follower Yoshihiro) Inoue to stop on the 19th but it turned out I lost against them," guru Shoko Asahara said in his first statement in the year-long trial. The gassing took place in the morning rush hour on March 20, 1995.
Twelve people were killed and more than 6,000 passengers fell ill in the nerve gas attack on five Tokyo subway lines.
Asahara, leader of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth) sect, also said the charge against him in the Tokyo subway case should be one of assault and not murder.
Asahara faces 16 other charges including several other murder charges and for masterminding a separate nerve gas attack.
"Basically this should be an assault charge," Asahara told Thursday's session at the Tokyo District Court. He did not elaborate.

It was Asahara's first clear statement in court since his trial opened in April 1996. He has been repeatedly removed from court for making incomprehensible statements but the judge gave him a chance on Thursday to enter his plea and add statements.
Despite his statement, he offered no clear plea on the charges.
